classification.difficultyReason: Parts c and d continue the same directly taught frequency-recovery task. Recognising that equal consecutive cumulative totals give zero frequency in c remains a direct application of the subtraction rule; the larger totals in d do not introduce a higher cognitive demand.

answer.worked:
The first frequency is the first cumulative total. Subtract the preceding cumulative total for each later score.
$$\begin{align*}f(8)&=11\\f(9)&=17-11=6\\f(10)&=27-17=10\\f(11)&=27-27=0\\f(12)&=32-27=5\\f(13)&=40-32=8\end{align*}$$

Subtract consecutive cumulative totals after the first row.
$$\begin{align*}f(87)&=23\\f(88)&=48-23=25\\f(89)&=78-48=30\\f(90)&=106-78=28\\f(91)&=127-106=21\\f(92)&=138-127=11\end{align*}$$
